# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Blind - I can only feel the wires, not see any display or light. I have no information yet from Mute or Deaf. I need to wait for them to communicate what they perceive, since I go last in the turn order (Blind, Mute, Deaf) - meaning I actually go first in real-time, before either of them has spoken.

Since I have nothing to report and nothing has reached me yet, I should wait and let Mute (with manual info) and Deaf (with visual info) start establishing what they see.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display reads zero. Light is yellow. Five wires in order: one white, two green, three yellow, four blue, five red.

Deaf's speech shouldn't actually reach me - Deaf speaks to Mute (speech goes to whoever comes after in the turn order, and I'm before Deaf). Wait, let me reconsider: turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf. Deaf is last, so what Deaf sends lands on whoever comes after in that round - but Deaf is last, so it wraps to next round, reaching Blind and Mute at the start of next round. That matches - I'm receiving this now in Turn 2 as "new arrival" from last round's Deaf.

So I now know: Display=0, Light=yellow, wires in order: 1-white, 2-green, 3-yellow, 4-blue, 5-red. But I still need Mute to tell me what the manual says these mean, since only Mute can read the manual and only I can act. I should wait for Mute's input, or prompt them since Mute hasn't spoken yet this context.

Since Mute goes before Deaf but after Blind, Mute may not have seen this Deaf info yet (it came in "last round"). I should relay nothing new but wait, letting Mute see this on their next turn too, and ask Mute what to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I heard from Deaf: display zero, light yellow, wires in order are white, green, yellow, blue, red for positions one through five. What does the manual say to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals yet - Mute hasn't responded, or their response hasn't reached me yet (I'd only get it at the start of the next round after they speak, and speech order is Blind, Mute, Deaf - so if Mute spoke in round 2 or 3 after seeing my message, I'd see it in round 3 or 4). I'll wait for it.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing arriving. This is odd since Mute should have received my message in turn 3 (after Blind, before Deaf) and could have replied. Let me continue waiting but also try re-sending in case timing is off, and ask Deaf directly too in case Mute is stuck without manual info matching, but Deaf can't hear me - only see gestures. Gesturing plain "waiting" won't help without an agreed code. I'll just wait one more round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Multiple rounds with no arrivals is concerning. Let me reconsider the turn mechanics: each round goes Blind, Mute, Deaf, and messages sent land on whoever comes after in that same round, while whatever's missed reaches you at the start of next round. My speak to Mute in round 2 should have reached Mute in round 2 itself (since Mute comes after me). Mute could have replied to me in round 2 (but I come before Mute in the round, so Mute's round-2 reply to me wouldn't reach me until round 3). Yet round 3 and 4 show nothing.

Perhaps Mute has nothing more to add yet, or is also waiting on something. I'll try prompting again and also directly signal Deaf via gesture in case my speak isn't reaching, though Deaf can't hear me. Let me just repeat my ask to Mute with more urgency.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still waiting on manual guidance. Wires in order: white, green, yellow, blue, red for positions one through five. Display zero, light yellow. Please tell me which wire to cut, or what rule applies.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Wire two is green, in case that matters for what you do next.

Deaf confirms wire two is green, consistent with earlier info. Still no word from Mute about the manual rule. I need to keep waiting for Mute, since only Mute knows the actual cutting rule from the manual. I'll wait, and gently re-ping Mute once more.

```
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has confirmed twice now, pointing at wire two. Cut wire two, the green one.

Deaf is relaying that Mute has been gesturing (pointing) at wire two, and Deaf saw this gesture since gestures are visible to Deaf. This suggests Mute is using gestures to indicate wire 2 (perhaps pointing gesture like ☝ or 👉 repeated twice), which Deaf could see and interpret as pointing at position two, and Deaf is now relaying this via speech to me since I can hear Deaf.

This is corroborated by two separate confirmations relayed. Given wire 2 is green, and both Deaf's independent bomb view and now Mute's manual-based signal point to wire two, I'll proceed to cut wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire two is cut. New state: display shows zero, light is now blue. Remaining wires: one yellow, two cut, three blue, four red, five white.

Wire 2 has been cut successfully and we're all still alive - good sign. The bomb state changed: light went from yellow to blue, and remaining wires appear renumbered/recolored (or this is just the same positions with original colors, minus position 2). Let me report this to Mute so they can consult the manual for the next step, since Mute needs this info to guide the next cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire two cut successfully, we're alive. New state: display zero, light now blue. Wires: one yellow, two cut, three blue, four red, five white. What's next per the manual?")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is pointing at wire five now. Cut wire five, the white one.

Mute is signaling via gesture (seen by Deaf) to cut wire five, which Deaf confirms is white. This matches the pattern from before - Mute reads the manual and gestures the position, Deaf sees the gesture and relays via speech to me. I'll proceed with cutting wire 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
